answer: Because the timing is written down against the sonnet challenge, the cipher audit can replay the fable history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm therefore has to pad 122 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 4 times over for the same share of the pool. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
